question_text: Figure shows vertical cross-sections of three ideal solid spheres $A$, $B$ and $C$ of equal masses, of radius $r$ and having thin walls. The spheres can be rotated about a vertical axis passing through respective centres. If $A$, $B$ and $C$ are made of materials of different densities, the rotational kinetic energies to be provided for same bodies if $A$, $B$ and $C$ attain equal angular speeds, which of the disc passing through its centre, all figures are drawn to the same scale. $KE_A$, $KE_B$, $KE_C$ respectively are the rotational kinetic energies to be provided to the bodies $A$, $B$ and $C$ to attain equal angular speeds.
